name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, serving as the primary gateway with the state's only airport and major railway station. Located on the Dhansiri River plains near the Assam border; base for exploring Kachari heritage and nearby nature sites.
facts: Only airport and major railhead in Nagaland
Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors from outside Nagaland
Elevation about 145 m on Dhansiri River plains

name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom dating to the 10th–13th centuries, featuring distinctive mushroom-domed monolithic sandstone pillars and fort remnants. Protected archaeological site in the heart of Dimapur.
facts: ASI-protected monument (N-NL-1)
Mushroom-shaped pillars up to 15 feet high
Remnants of pre-13th century Dimasa Kachari capital
Easily accessible in central Dimapur

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Historic Digambara Jain temple established in 1947, featuring ornate architecture with intricate glass work. Primary deity is Lord Mahavira; serves as an important spiritual and cultural landmark for the Jain community in Dimapur.
facts: Built in 1947 by Sethi families who relocated from Kohima during WWII
Located on Jain Temple Road near SD Jain institutions
Moolnayak is Lord Mahavira
One of the few major Jain temples in Nagaland

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum behind Naga Shopping Arcade promoting informal science education through galleries on senses, children's exhibits, and fun science. Includes a planetarium and outdoor science park.
facts: Inaugurated in 2004 by then CM Neiphiu Rio
Closed on Mondays; open 10 AM–4 PM otherwise
Entry fee nominal (around ₹10)
Near Kachari Ruins and Super Market Lane

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Dimapur’s best-known flea market and shopping hub, packed with imported clothing, footwear, electronics, and bargains from Myanmar, Thailand, and China. A lively commercial and tourist attraction in central Dimapur.
facts: Originated from Tibetan trader stalls in the early 1980s
Known for affordable imported goods and bargaining
Popular with both locals and tourists
Located in the heart of Dimapur near NST Colony area

name: Diezephe Craft Village
description: Artisan village about 13 km from Dimapur (near Chümoukedima) specializing in traditional Naga woodcarving, bamboo and cane work, and loin-loom weaving. Recognized as a Best Tourism Village; supports local crafts and offers homestays.
facts: Promoted by Nagaland Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation
Tenyimei artisans skilled in wood carving and weaving
Awarded as Best Tourism Village (bronze) 2023
Note: now under Chümoukedima district following 2021 split from Dimapur

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre stone garden and museum near the airport and railway station, showcasing regional cultural exhibits and open-air stone installations. Popular short stop for visitors.
facts: Located ~3 km from railway station and 500 m from airport
Average daily footfall 20, higher on weekends
Part of North East Zone Cultural Centre network
Official site on dimapur.nic.in places of interest

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped park inside the State Horticulture Nursery area offering boating, picnic spots, and family recreation. A green oasis in Dimapur popular during peak tourist months.
facts: Located within State Horticulture Nursery
Features boating and ziplining options
Peak season November–January with higher footfall
Listed on official Dimapur places of interest

name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and major hill station at about 1,444 m elevation. Historic Angami Naga settlement that became the scene of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima; base for Hornbill Festival, war heritage, and highland treks.
facts: State capital since 1963
Elevation approximately 1,444 m
Requires Inner Line Permit for non-residents
Nearest airport and railhead at Dimapur (74 km)

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials and a memorial to 917 cremated Hindu and Sikh soldiers; famous epitaph and preserved tennis court site of close-quarters fighting.
facts: Maintained by Commonwealth War Graves Commission
Epitaph: 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'
Open daily approximately 09:00–16:00
Located in central Kohima on the former Deputy Commissioner's bungalow grounds

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Open-air cultural village between Kigwema and Phesama, 12 km south of Kohima, featuring traditional morungs of all Naga tribes. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (1–10 December).
facts: Name derived from Kigwema and Phesama villages
Houses morungs representing Nagaland's tribes
Hornbill Festival venue since 2000
Located on NH-29 / Asian Highway 1

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village 20 km west of Kohima, declared India's first Green Village in 2005. Known for terraced paddy fields, community conservation, Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan, and historic resistance against British forces.
facts: India's first Green Village (2005)
Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary covers ~30–70 sq km
Elevation about 1,621 m
Angami warrior history including battles against British 1830–1880

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude alpine valley (2,438–2,452 m) straddling the Kohima (Nagaland) and Senapati (Manipur) border behind Japfu Peak. Famous for rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers including the rare Dzukou Lily, and popular multi-day treks.
facts: Known as Valley of Flowers of the Northeast
Elevation floor ~2,438–2,452 m
Accessible mainly via Viswema or Jakhama trailheads from Kohima side
Border note: core valley shared with Manipur's Senapati district

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m, part of the Barail Range about 15 km south of Kohima. Famous for panoramic views, winter snow, and the world's tallest rhododendron tree (Guinness record). Popular moderate-to-challenging trek.
facts: Elevation 3,048 m (second highest in Nagaland after Saramati)
Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree (~20–30 m)
Best trekking season November–March
Trail typically starts from Kigwema or nearby villages

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State ethnographic museum on Bayavü Hill, Kohima, displaying traditional Naga textiles, ornaments, weapons, musical instruments, and models of tribal houses across multiple galleries. Opened in 1970 by the Department of Art and Culture.
facts: Established and opened to public 25 November 1970
Located on Upper Bayavü Hill
Showcases artefacts from all major Naga tribes
Useful introduction before visiting villages

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Cathedral of the Diocese of Kohima, noted for architecture blending traditional Naga house elements with modern design. Features a large carved wooden crucifix; construction largely funded by Japanese donors in memory of soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima.
facts: Consecrated January 1991
Capacity around 4,500
16-foot carved wooden crucifix among Asia's largest
Located on Aradura Hill with views over Kohima

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small Angami Naga eco-tourism village in the Western Angami highlands of Kohima District at about 2,130 m. Community-run homestays, hunting ban since 1999, and focus on birdwatching, trekking, and low-impact tourism with a development fund from visitor income.
facts: Population ~156 (2011)
Hunting and trapping banned since 1999
Dzüleke Eco-Tourism Board and Development Fund
About 30–40 km from Kohima via Khonoma route

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run heritage tourist village about 36–41 km from Kohima, recreating traditional Angami Naga architecture with thatched cottages, cultural performances, local cuisine, and a small ethnographic museum. Model for rural homestay tourism.
facts: Established around 2001–2002 as community tourism project
Traditional huts for overnight stays
Cultural evenings and Naga cuisine including rice beer
Accessible via road from Kohima towards Wokha/Botsa
